idiom_name: Exposed json() / jsonb() column with kotlinx.serialization
implementation_notes: The exposed-json module adds json()/jsonb() column factories: hand the factory a @Serializable type plus a Json configuration (or a Jackson serializer/deserializer pair) and Exposed converts values around the column, mapping to JSON/JSONB on PostgreSQL, JSON on MySQL/H2, TEXT on SQLite and NVARCHAR(MAX) on SQL Server. The KSerializer is resolved from the type, so no hand-written mapper exists, and functions such as extract()/contains() keep the payload queryable where the dialect allows it. Use an ordinary table mapping when the fields must take part in joins or constraints.
pitfalls: Json configuration decides compatibility: a strict instance (no ignoreUnknownKeys, encodeDefaults) throws on rows written by older or newer models - freeze the configuration alongside the format version.
SQLite jsonb columns are stored as BLOBs wrapped in JSONB(), so a codec that expects JSON text must not read the raw value (Exposed's castToJsonFormat covers the default path).
Only @Serializable types (or explicitly supplied serializers) work, so framework-managed entities convert to plain data classes first.
